svg.title: Qure.ai Life Sciences CRM — First-time Dashboard Guide
svg.desc: A Qure.ai themed poster explaining how to navigate the India Life Sciences CRM dashboard and turn metrics into actions.
svg.text: Qure.ai Life Sciences CRM
FIRST-TIME DASHBOARD GUIDE · INDIA FOCUS · TURN RESEARCH INTO PRIORITISED NEXT ACTIONS
Start with the operating snapshot
The top-left KPI block answers: How large is the market list, where is attention needed, and how reliable is the research?
CORAL = attention / decision needed · TEAL = confirmed, current, or progressing · slate = context or research detail
1. Read patterns, not isolated numbers
Leads by sector
Example: 88 pharma contacts vs. 12 biotech contacts.
Insight: pharma is the current relationship base. Build biotech coverage deliberately, not reactively.
Leads by seniority
Use the executive mix to plan stakeholder coverage.
Insight: pair an economic buyer with a technical evaluator before proposing a use case.
Leads by solution interest
Example: RWE / commercial evidence currently dominates the tagged use cases.
Insight: convert the signal into a focused RWE value proposition and supporting proof points.
TIP: A high count indicates research concentration — not confirmed demand, deal probability, or permission to contact.
NEWS LENS: Log trial readouts, launches, partnerships, and regulatory updates as source-backed context before changing a hypothesis.
2. Turn the dashboard into a weekly workflow

g.text: Filter Tier 1 accounts, high lead scores, and overdue next steps.
Check verification status and source date before a role-specific approach.
Log the next best action, owner, due date, and outcome in Activities.
Update the opportunity stage only when new research or relevant news changes the account hypothesis.

svg.text: A clean decision rule
If the role is unverified, recheck it. If account coverage is thin, research the stakeholder map. If the use case is clear, book the next action. If evidence is missing, do not advance the stage.
QURE.AI INTERNAL OPERATING GUIDE · RESEARCH SNAPSHOT, NOT A REVENUE FORECAST
